content:
The image shows small green banana fruits with dark brown-black necrotic lesions at the distal (blossom/finger) end of the fruit. This is a classic presentation of Cigar End Rot, where the tip of the banana fruit develops a dry, dark, cigar-like rot. The lesions are confined to the fruit tip area and show the characteristic dark necrosis spreading inward.

This does not match Panama Disease (which affects vascular tissue/leaves/pseudostem, not fruit surface). It doesn't match Sigatoka (leaf disease), Cordana Leaf Spot (leaves), Anthracnose (typically post-harvest surface lesions), or Bunchy Top (leaf/plant architecture).
